He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State Redhawks]], the [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara Broncos]], and the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. ==High school career== Eaddy played basketball at [[Notre Dame High School (West Haven, Connecticut)|Notre Dame High School]] in [[West Haven, Connecticut]] for three years. He moved to Tennessee Preparatory Academy in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] for his senior year. Eaddy averaged 24.6 points and was named MVP of the National Association of Christian Athletes Elite Division. He attended The Skill Factory in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]] for a prep year. He committed to playing college basketball for [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].{{cite web |last1=Borges |first1=David |title=Notre Dame-West Haven coach Jason Shea not surprised by Tahj Eaddy's college success |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/nhregister/article/Notre-Dame-West-Haven-coach-Jason-Shea-not-15154807.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=March 24, 2020}} ==College career== As a freshman at Southeast Missouri State, Eaddy averaged 7.5 points and shot a team-high 42 percent from three-point range.{{cite web |last1=Kartje |first1=Ryan |title=Point guard Tahj Eaddy has found the ideal situation at USC |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2021-02-20/usc-basketball-tahj-eaddy-scoring-surge |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}} For his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]]. After sitting out for one year due to NCAA transfer rules, Eaddy averaged 15 points and 3.2 assists per game, earning Second Team All-[[West Coast Conference]] honors.{{cite web |last1=Borges |first1=David |title=Tahj Eaddy, USC's point guard and a West Haven product, returns 'home' this week to Bubbleville |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/uconn/nhregister/article/Tahj-Eaddy-USC-s-point-guard-and-a-West-Haven-15761945.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=November 29, 2020}} He scored a season-high 30 points in a 68–56 win over [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]] on January 3, 2019.{{cite web |title=Eaddy has career night, leads Santa Clara past San Diego |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/01/04/eaddy-has-career-night-leads-santa-clara-past-san-diego/38840913/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=January 4, 2019}} During his junior season, Eaddy received less playing time and averaged 9.1 points. He transferred to [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] for his senior season as a graduate transfer.{{cite web |last1=Grosbard |first1=Adam |title=Grad transfer Tahj Eaddy providing steadying presence for USC men's basketball |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2021/01/18/grad-transfer-tahj-eaddy-providing-steadying-presence-for-usc-mens-basketball/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=January 18, 2021}} On February 13, 2021, Eaddy scored 29 points in a 76–65 win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].{{cite web |last1=Zemek |first1=Matt |title=Tahj Eaddy, with 29 points vs Washington State, approaches star status |url=https://trojanswire.usatoday.com/2021/02/14/tahj-eaddy-with-29-points-vs-washington-state-approaches-star-status-for-usc-trojans/ |website=Trojans Wire |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=February 14, 2021}} As a senior, Eaddy averaged 13.6 points, 2.9 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=Wadleigh |first1=Matt |title=Tahj Eaddy signs with the Orlando Magic |url=https://trojanswire.usatoday.com/2021/07/31/usc-trojans-basketball-star-tahj-eaddy-signs-with-the-orlando-magic/ |access-date=September 18, 2021 |work=Trojans Wire |date=July 31, 2021}} He was named to the Second Team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]]. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] instead of taking advantage of the NCAA's offer of an additional year of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Kartje |first1=Ryan |title=Tahj Eaddy will forgo final year at USC and declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2021-04-08/tahu-eaddy-usc-declare-for-2021-nba-draft |access-date=September 18, 2021 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 8, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Eaddy signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] for the Summer League in Las Vegas. Eaddy was drafted with the first pick in the second round by the [[Raptors 905]] in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]].{{Cite web|title=2021 NBA G League Draft Board|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2021-nba-g-league-draft-order/|access-date=2021-10-23|website=NBA G League|language=en-US}} However he did not make the final roster.{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Blake |title=Raptors 905: 10 storylines to follow for 2021-22 G League season |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-905-10-storylines-follow-2021-22-g-league-season/ |access-date=November 12, 2021 |work=Sportsnet.ca |date=November 5, 2021}} On December 17, 2021, Eaddy signed with [[BC Prienai]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]].{{cite web |title="Labas GAS" gynėjų grandyje – naujokas iš dukterinės NBA lygos |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-162028-labas-gas-gyneju-grandyje-naujokas-is-dukterines-nba-lygos.html |website=Basketnews.lt |access-date=February 27, 2022 |language=Lithuanian |date=December 17, 2021}} In 17 games, he averaged 9.2 points, 1.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists per contest, shooting with 44% from beyond the 3-point arc. Eaddy started the 2022–23 season with the Slovak club [[BKM Lučenec|Lučenec]]. In 21 games, he averaged 18.1 points, 2.2 rebounds and 3.6 assists per contest, shooting with 45% from beyond the 3-point arc. On March 17, 2023, Eaddy moved to Greek club [[G.S. Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] for the rest of the season. In 4 league games, he averaged 7.5 points, 2.5 rebounds and 3.2 assists, playing around 19 minutes per contest.
